blocks.text: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are usually caused by bacteria, most commonly Escherichia coli. These bacteria enter the urinary system through urethra and infect the bladder, ureters, or kidneys.

The symptoms of a UTI include a frequent and urgent need to urinate, pain or burning during urination, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, lower abdominal pain, and sometimes fever or chills. Treatment involves a course of antibiotics to kill the causative bacteria. Drinking plenty of water and urinating frequently can also help to flush out the bacteria and alleviate symptoms.
